items.title: 60499_Garvin Bushell oral history interview
items.q: But one German evidently had too many drinks and he came right up into the crowd...

ctx.x: What year was this, Mr. Bushell?

1925, May 3 or 6th, something like that. And everybody was commenting and saying how well we performed, how much they loved our work, and saying what a great show it was. But one German evidently had too many drinks and he came right up into the crowd and tore open his shirt and said, 'I'm a German to my heart. I don't understand why the government allows these black people to come to our country. During the war they cut off our noses, they cut off our ears,' he's speaking about the Senegalese, you know.
